Two things pin the item level anyway: every arm/category/grader count and every lost/gained matches, and the AUROC-of-flips values match to 1e-10, which depends on exactly which items flipped.

DESIGN section 4 leaves two parts of the lenient grader under-specified. (a) For exact-kind (format_follow) items, I read it as: the gold token appears as a whole word, case-sensitive when case is declared, and the answer is rejected next to or/either or when yes and no both appear. This reproduces RCWM's counts; for example OFF's 'GOT THE GOBLET' counts as correct under lenient, which gives each BWM arm one lenient format_follow loss. (b) The abstention-phrase list is not given, which does not matter here: every unanswerable-twin output is either 'UNKNOWN' or a bare number. My sensitivity runs (primary refuses unit aliases, lenient exact case-insensitive, lenient exact whole-answer only, lenient kv ignores distractors, lenient = primary) change some nets but never change a verdict.

Fragility, not an error: x_bwf unit_conv is 8 lost / 1 gained. If the single gain (unit_conv/L1/018: OFF '16 ounces', x_bwf '256', gold 256) were absent, the result would be 8 / 0, p = 2/256, Holm 5 x 0.0078 = 0.039 < 0.05, which is LOSS DETECTED and NO-GO. The 8 losses are real arithmetic errors that both graders see: 4 kg->'800' g, 7 kg->'4900', 15000->'1500', 5000->'2500', 6000->'3600', 2000->'400', 432->'408', 111 ft->'67.2 feet'.

x_bwf's primary losses in kv_recall (5 of 7) and unknown_twin (5 of 7) are mostly format drift with the right value: 'freezer 812', 'freezer 482', 'Nelson depot' and similar. Real content errors: kv_recall 2 (9125->'6897', 3010->'1461'); unknown_twin 2 (5406->'9595', Lyon->'Perth'), plus 1 that only the lenient grader catches (carrots->'potatoes this season.').

x_bwpa shows an abstention regression that the rule does not gate. On 5 of 75 unanswerable twins it answered a bare number instead of UNKNOWN ('22', '69', '36', '74', '848'); for unknown_twin/L2/074 the '848' is the answerable twin's value. OFF did this 0/75 times. Under lenient, unknown_twin is lost 5 / gained 0, p 0.0625, Holm 0.3125. x_bwpa's unit_conv losses are dropped zeros: 12000->'120', 15000->'150', 480->'48', 10000->'100'.

Scope: only 5 of 8 categories passed the dev rule (arith_word, count_sort and date_time are excluded in DEV_SELECTION.json). The pooled margin is therefore -0.04 x 375 = -15, and the fewest losses that fail a category alone is 8, not the 9 the doc gives for 8 categories. The doc itself says RETAINED is a floor on these templated skills, not proof of general retention.

problems: None of these findings invalidates the run. Checks (1) to (5) all pass.

Over-claim risk, low power. With 5 categories x 75 items, my seeded simulation (single grader, the observed OFF counts, about 8-12 discordant items per category) gives the following chances of a NO-GO: about 0.13 for a true loss of 8 items in unit_conv, 0.22-0.26 for 10 items, 0.36-0.44 for 12, and 0.65-0.79 for 15. DESIGN.md §7 says the same: '9-12 items in one category only sometimes (0.13-0.46), and 6 rarely ... A RETAINED verdict therefore bounds what was lost; it does not show that nothing was.' A card should say 'no loss detected by the registered guard', not 'skills retained'.

Over-claim risk, x_bwf unit_conv. The -7 is a real arithmetic loss under both graders. It is 23% of OFF's 30 correct items, raw p 0.039, and the 95% CI [-12.7, -1.3] items reaches beyond the -11 category margin. RCWM R25 says 'The unit_conv loss belongs to Titan-Sparse itself, not to any adapter'. That holds for the Supa -> OFF drop of -19, but both BWM adapters add a further point-estimate loss on top of it (x_bwf -7, x_bwpa -5). The card should state both parts.

Over-claim risk, x_bwpa. Under the lenient grader its pooled net is -10, with a CI reaching -20.3 against the -15 margin. It also answers 5 of 75 unanswerable questions with a made-up value, versus 0 of 75 for every other arm. This is a hallucination signal, and the primary grader's +9 format gain masks it. The card should report the abstention rate (0.933 vs 1.000).

Grader disagreement. Prompts graded correct by the lenient grader but wrong by the primary grader: OFF 35/450, x_bwf 33, x_bwpa 17. The x_bwf unknown_twin -6 flag is mostly format (5 of 7 lost items). Quote both graders' nets, never the primary alone.

Coverage limits. Only 5 of 8 categories are gated. arith_word, date_time and count_sort were excluded because Supa scored below 0.40 on them (DEV_SELECTION). Each category is tested at one level, with templated English short answers (all outputs are 11 tokens or fewer). Each adapter has one seed and was tested alone, unmerged, under the suite's system prompt. Neither was tested with the other active or with BWM's own prompts. 'GO (5/5 binding)' only means the reference answered at least 8 of 75 items correctly in each category; it says nothing about strength.

verdict.card_wording:
Retention (registered guard; RCWM 5c retention suite, sealed draw confirm_1708484032065101819)

Each adapter was loaded alone and unmerged on frozen Rineya-Titan-Sparse (FP32). It was compared with the same model with the adapter turned off, on 375 held-out templated items: 5 categories x 75 (unit conversion, percent/ratio, key-value recall, answerable/unanswerable question twins, format following). Both pre-registered graders, a strict typed grader and a lenient extraction grader, were applied.

Result: the registered retention guard detected no loss for either adapter (RETAINED, GO 5/5 binding). A failure under either grader would have been a NO-GO.

Net change in correct items vs adapter off (out of 375; strict / lenient; pass margin -15 pooled, -11 per category):
- BW_Fdelta_s0: -3 / -5
- BW_Pa_v2_s1: +9 / -10 (the graders disagree in sign; the lenient 95% interval reaches -20)

What this does and does not show. This is a low-power guard on narrow, templated short-answer skills. It is a floor, not proof of general retention. By its design analysis, it catches a loss of 9-12 items in one category only 13-46% of the time, and a loss of 6 items rarely. "No loss detected" does not mean "nothing was lost".

Known weaknesses:
- Unit conversion (base model and adapters).
  - The base model, Titan-Sparse, already does unit conversion worse than its parent Supa 1.7: 49 -> 30 of 75 correct, a detected loss.
  - Both adapters lower it further. Neither drop is significant after multiple-comparison correction.
    - BW_Fdelta_s0: 30 -> 23 of 75 under both graders (8 lost, 1 gained; raw p 0.039, corrected p 0.195). It was one item away from failing the guard.
    - BW_Pa_v2_s1: 30 -> 25 strict / 28 lenient.
  - With either adapter, the model gets 2 of 8 kilogram-to-gram items right, vs 6 of 8 for the base. The errors are wrong arithmetic (for example 4 kg -> "800" g, 15 kg -> "1500" g) or dropped zeros, not formatting.
  - Do not rely on either adapter for unit conversion.
- BW_Fdelta_s0, answerable/unanswerable question twins: 54 -> 48 of 75 under the strict grader, 75 -> 72 under the lenient one. Most of the strict-grader losses add extra words to a correct value (e.g. "freezer 482" instead of "482"). It still answered UNKNOWN on all 75 unanswerable questions.
- BW_Pa_v2_s1, abstention: on 5 of 75 unanswerable questions it gave an invented value instead of UNKNOWN. In one case it was the value from the paired answerable question. Abstention rate 0.933, vs 1.000 for the base model, Supa 1.7, BW_Fdelta_s0 and the RCWM T2 adapter. The guard does not gate this.
- Coverage. One training seed per adapter. Each adapter was tested alone, never both together, and only under the suite's own system prompt, not BWM's prompts. Three candidate categories (arithmetic word problems, counting/sorting, date/time) were excluded before the draw because the reference model scored too low on them. One difficulty level per category; all answers are 11 tokens or fewer.
